director.question: q1
director.why: q1 offers the highest information gain at 0.155 bits and directly tests Ia fading versus TDE plateau in g-band.

question.text: Brighter in r three days from now than at its last r detection?

risky.text: Brighter than 35 microjansky in g 4 days from now?

payload.rule: Every ZTF g or r measurement taken after this bet was sealed, up to one day past its last forecast, is scored against the forecast, interpolated linearly between days. The question is settled by the first r measurement within a day of its time; a limit above the reference leaves it void.

instrument.why: Multi-night g/r/i detections spanning ~26 days at stable ~19.5-20.8 mag with no single-night spike or erratic jumps indicate a persistent sky source, not detector noise.

implausible.why: Peak 29 days ago is incompatible with the observed ~1 mag brightening over the following 26 days because Type II supernovae rise in days then plateau or decline and do not rise monotonically for weeks

Peak 30 days ago is incompatible with steady brightening to the present because stripped-envelope supernovae rise in 10 to 20 days then decline quickly and cannot keep rising for a month past maximum.

theories.argument: The g/r/i light curve rises over ~16 days to a peak around day -9 and then fades ~0.5 mag in g over the next 10 days, fit by a z=0.2 broad x1=2.8 normal-color SN Ia with chi2 per point 0.58 and model weight 0.83. The blue near-peak color and high-latitude location with deep pre-explosion limits are exactly as expected for an extragalactic thermonuclear explosion.

refuted_if.why: A SN Ia 13 days past peak must continue fading in g, so remaining at peak-like brightness would violate the template decline.

theories.weakest_point: The r-band stays essentially flat near 20 mag from day -18 to day 0 with sparse sampling and shallow limits around day -10 to -8, allowing a slower plateau that is atypical for even a broad SN Ia.

theories.argument: The transient shows a slow month-long rise of about one magnitude to a blue plateau near 19.9 mag with g-r near zero and stable emission well matched by a 10000 K blackbody at chi2 0.39 per point. High Galactic latitude and a real PSF-like difference source support an extragalactic long-lived blue transient with little cooling.

refuted_if.why: A TDE should remain on a slow month-scale blue plateau near peak so halving to half-light in four days is too fast.

theories.weakest_point: The brightening is low-amplitude and sparsely sampled with no confirmed host nucleus and only modest blue color.

theories.argument: The source appeared after deep limits near 20.4 mag and persisted for ~26 days near 19.8-20.2 mag with g-r near 0.1 and similar i-band, consistent with a broad stripped-envelope photosphere. The Ib/c fit gives chi2 per point 1.8 with a real PSF-like stamp at b=-45 deg supporting an extragalactic supernova origin.

refuted_if.why: At about 35 days after the fitted peak an Ib/c must be fading on the cobalt tail, so r-band still near 43 uJy would rule out the expected decline.

theories.weakest_point: The fit needs z=0.005 which makes M about -12, many magnitudes too faint for a normal Ib/c, and it predicts peak at minus 30 days while the light curve stays flat for 25 days.

wording.text: It is about as likely as not that the distant flash will still be brighter than the set limit in green light 4 days from now.
